KEY MESSAGE 1...Frontal passage tonight into tomorrow morning brings 
scattered showers and gusty southwest winds, especially over far 
southeastern Massachusetts, Cape Cod, and the Islands.

The rest of today is largely dry outside of a sct'd warm advection 
shower, as yesterday's cold front lifts back to the northeast, this 
time as a warm front. A robust LLJ advects higher moisture into 
southern New England as well, with PWATs climbing to near 2.0 inches 
after 00z. Thus, there remains a low chance for showers throughout 
this evening. Given the added cloud cover and winds overnight, 
expecting a mild night with lows ranging from the upper 60s to lower 
70s.

As the cold front approaches overnight, additional showers move into 
the region during the predawn hours of Thursday, mainly 4-7 AM. 
However, dynamics are lacking as the front reaches southern New 
England. While there is a moisture-rich environment, the lack of 
ideal forcing means rainfall isn't expected to be widespread or 
necessarily heavy.

The wind will be more noticeable. As we've mentioned over the past 
day or so, there is a robust LLJ with winds aloft ranging between 45 
and 55 kt. While mixing will be limited inland due to the nocturnal 
inversion, there should be enough mixing to allow gusts across the 
interior to range between 20 and 30 MPH. Along and east of I-95, 
gusts of 30-40 MPH remain possible, with a small area mainly near 
the Cape and far southeastern Massachusetts where 40+ MPH isn't out 
of the question prior to sunrise. Throughout the day Thursday, wind 
direction shifts more to the west, with gusts ranging from 20 to 30 
MPH.

Currently, we feel the greatest impacts will be for the marine 
community. Gale Warnings are in effect around the Cape and Islands 
for those stronger winds. By Thursday afternoon, the surface cold 
front is offshore. However, temperatures aloft are slower to lower, 
so it will still be fairly seasonable Thursday afternoon. Then comes 
a reinforcement of colder air Thursday night, with 925 mb 
temperatures falling from around +20C Thursday to +10C Friday.

KEY MESSAGE 2...Dry weather, comfortable humidities and light 
onshore winds Friday through Saturday night. Cool nighttime low 
temperatures Friday night. 

Forecast for Friday into Saturday remains consistent in showing a 
large high pressure area coming in from the eastern Great Lakes and 
southeast Ontario Friday, then settling over the Northeast Friday 
evening before moving offshore Saturday. This will bring dry and 
pleasant weather conditions to Southern New England, with seasonably 
mild days with full sun during the daytime hours Friday and Saturday 
but a cool Friday night due to strong radiational cooling. Some of 
the more typical sites which radiate well under clear skies and 
light winds could see low temperatures drop into the mid 40s, 
including areas around I-495, NW MA and Martha's Vineyard. High 
temperatures in the mid 70s, with lower 70s near the Cape and 
Islands. Conditions look favorable for outdoor plans Friday and 
Saturday. 

KEY MESSAGE 3...Frontal boundary Sunday brings increased 
humidity and chances for rain Sunday afternoon and evening. 

The high pressure moving eastward allows for an increasingly moist 
airmass ahead of a cold frontal boundary which arrives Sunday 
afternoon into Sunday evening. Most models show increasing rain 
chances centered around Sunday afternoon or into the evening. While 
there are good chances for rain in this Sunday afternoon to Sunday 
evening timeframe, there is more uncertainty in terms of how much 
rain falls. It looks as though the placement of the greatest 
rainfall seems confined to the South Coast, Cape Cod and the 
Islands. While it looks as though Sunday evening looks wet for these 
areas, we're not expecting rainfall to become especially heavy as 
the frontal boundary looks progressive. 

KEY MESSAGE 4...High pressure returns for early next week, 
bringing a return to seasonable temperatures and low humidities.

Behind the frontal boundary Sunday night, high pressure from Canada 
builds back in, bringing seasonable temperatures, dry weather and 
low levels of humidity for the early part of next week. The 
potential exists for a couple of cooler nights Monday night and 
Tuesday night with high pressure in the vicinity.
